newsitem.title: UK: Daily Mail takes Teletext stake to 75 pct.
newsitem.headline: Daily Mail takes Teletext stake to 75 pct.

text.p: Britain's Daily Mail and General Trust Plc said on Friday that it had agreed to acquire a further 30 percent stake in Teletext Holdings Ltd for 25 million stg, lifting its total interest to 75 percent.
Daily Mail is acquiring the shares from Philips Electronics UK Limited, the British arm of Dutch giant Philips NV.
Put and call option arrangements for the remaining 15 percent of Philips' Teletext shareholding have been agreed for an additional consideration of up to 15 million stg.

However, a Daily Mail spokesman said that Philips was expected to retain its stake in Teletext for the foreseeable future. It has also agreed to continue to provide technical advice and support to Teletext.
Venture capital firm Media Ventures holds the remaining 10 percent stake in London-based Teletext, which operates the text news services on Britain's ITV and Channel 4.
Teletext made pre-tax profit of 13.8 million stg on turnover of 34.8 million in 1995.
Teletext chairman and Daily Mail director Sir David English said that the electronic media world was poised to enter a phase of rapid development.
"Teletext will be better able to seize opportunities in this challenging future by having a strong media group such as DMGT as its controlling shareholder," he said.

"Philips' contribution to the development of Teletext has been invaluable and we are delighted that they have agreed to continue to provide their technical know-how to the company and to remain a significant shareholder."
